notes: Segmenting into blocks was easy; the lookup of each letter was the slow part, since the consonant pairings are arbitrary and several sit close to a misleading natural value (g, k, d, s, m, h, n, t all map to a block that reads as a different consonant in real Hangul). Most error-prone were w, y and x acting as vowels (darwin, rhythm, xylophone), the tense initials for p, q, t, v, z, and vowel runs such as yield and queue. In decoding I did not read the forms as words at sight; each one became recognisable partway through, usually after three or four letters, and the rest then served as confirmation rather than as fresh lookup.
